module_title: Intermediate Tech - Cloud Service Models, ML, and IoT Sensors
introduction: This tier breaks down the operational delivery models of cloud computing (SaaS, PaaS, IaaS), introduces Machine Learning as a critical subset of AI, and explains how IoT devices actually gather data from the physical world.

core_concepts.title: SaaS (Software as a Service)
core_concepts.description:
The most common cloud model for normal users. Instead of downloading and installing software, you access it directly through a web browser. 
Examples: Gmail, Facebook, Microsoft Office 365.

core_concepts.title: PaaS and IaaS
core_concepts.description:
- **PaaS (Platform as a Service)**: Provides developers with a framework and tools to build, test, and deploy their own apps over the internet.
- **IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service)**: Allows big businesses to rent virtual servers, networks, and raw data storage from cloud providers instead of buying their own physical hardware.

core_concepts.title: Machine Learning (ML)
core_concepts.description:
A specific subfield of AI. Instead of explicitly programming a computer with strict rules, we feed it massive amounts of 'Data'. The computer uses algorithms to find patterns in that data and 'learns' on its own. 
Examples: YouTube or Netflix video recommendations, spam email filtering.

core_concepts.title: Sensors in IoT
core_concepts.description: Because IoT devices operate without human intervention, they rely heavily on 'Sensors' to collect real-time data from their environment (e.g., Temperature sensors in a smart AC, or motion sensors in a smart security camera).

important_entities.name: Smart Home Architecture
important_entities.significance: A residence where lighting, heating, TVs, and security cameras are interconnected via Wi-Fi and can be controlled remotely by a smartphone. This is the most frequently tested practical example of IoT.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will test if you know the difference. **Rule:** They are not synonyms. Artificial Intelligence is the broad, overarching concept (the umbrella). Machine Learning is a specific application *underneath* that umbrella. AI is the goal; ML is the method.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the hierarchy: Software is for end-users, Platform is for app developers, Infrastructure is for IT system administrators.

exam_strategy_tips: In statement-based questions, you will often be asked to classify an application. Always remember that Google Drive and Gmail are classic examples of SaaS (Software as a Service).
